bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Soak dry Calamus rattan flat reed in warm water (90 to 105 degrees Fahrenheit) for 5 to 10 minutes until fibers bend 180 degrees without cracking.
core_mechanism_bullets: Soak dry Calamus rattan flat reed in warm water (90 to 105 degrees Fahrenheit) for 5 to 10 minutes until fibers bend 180 degrees without cracking.
Always cut reed splints and stakes away from the body using heavy-duty basket shears and sand fibery edges smooth before weaving.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: Over-soaking reed beyond 20 minutes causes lignin swelling and gray mildew staining, while weaving bone-dry reed snaps the outer silica rind.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Compare the bend radius of dry flat reed vs reed soaked for 5 minutes in warm water, checking the smooth right side vs the fibrous wrong side.

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Basketry divides into four structural families of Plaiting (90-degree strips), Wicker (weft over rigid spokes), Twining, and Coiling.
core_mechanism_bullets: Basketry divides into four structural families of Plaiting (90-degree strips), Wicker (weft over rigid spokes), Twining, and Coiling.
Two-strand twining twists a pair of flexible weavers a half-turn (180 degrees) between each vertical stake to lock rows tightly in place.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: A square market basket uses a flat plaited checkerboard base, whereas a round berry basket radiates rigid round reed spokes in a wicker weave.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Examine four sample weave cards to identify over-one-under-one plain plaiting, diagonal twill, two-strand twining, and stitched coiled bundles.

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Continuous single-weaver round baskets require an odd number of vertical spokes (11, 13, or 15) so the over-under pattern alternates each circuit.
core_mechanism_bullets: Continuous single-weaver round baskets require an odd number of vertical spokes (11, 13, or 15) so the over-under pattern alternates each circuit.
An even number of vertical spokes requires either two alternating weavers (chase weaving) or a stop-and-start overlap splice on every row.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: When laying out a 5-by-5 square basket base with 1/2-inch flat reed, adding one extra center spoke on one side creates 19 total uprights for continuous weaving.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Weave 3 rows around a 6-spoke even jig vs a 7-spoke odd jig to prove why continuous single-strand weaving requires an odd spoke count.
bespoke_clusters.real_world_connection_box: Odd-Spoke Continuous Rim Weave and Base Slotting Standard: Continuous single-weaver round baskets require an odd number of vertical spokes (11, 13, or 15) so the over-under pattern alternates each circuit. An even number of vertical spokes requires either two alternating weavers (chase weaving) or a stop-and-start overlap splice on every row.

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Finish basket rims by folding unused spoke ends over the top row and binding a heavy oval rim reed inside and out with whip-stitch lashing.
core_mechanism_bullets: Finish basket rims by folding unused spoke ends over the top row and binding a heavy oval rim reed inside and out with whip-stitch lashing.
Campstool seats use a two-layer warp and weft wrap woven in an over-two, under-two diagonal twill (herringbone) pattern for load distribution.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: Stepping each row's over-two, under-two start by one warp strand to the right generates the classic 45-degree diagonal twill pattern on a hardwood stool frame.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Practice a 3-minute over-two, under-two diagonal twill weave on a 6-strand cardboard loom and demonstrate a tucked whip-stitch rim lock.
bespoke_clusters.real_world_connection_box: Rim Lashing and Diagonal Herringbone Campstool Seat Standard: Finish basket rims by folding unused spoke ends over the top row and binding a heavy oval rim reed inside and out with whip-stitch lashing. Campstool seats use a two-layer warp and weft wrap woven in an over-two, under-two diagonal twill (herringbone) pattern for load distribution.
